A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AsymRE research, with matching objectives, theoretical framework and original experiments. The main text, figures, equations and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit simulations and MATH fine-tuning experiments with Llama 8B and Qwen 3B, including training dynamics, entropy analyses and repeated-run collapse checks.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Llama 3B experiments, NuminaMath evaluations and direct comparisons with GRPO.

M1.justification: The AsymRE objective, context-corrected baseline and delayed behavior-policy updates remain unchanged. The added model and dataset experiments apply the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on competition-level NuminaMath problems in Section 5.2 and Appendix C, substantially extending real-data coverage beyond MATH. The original bandit and MATH tasks remain.

E2.justification: GRPO changes from a cited method to an evaluated comparator. v2 Figures 5 right and 13 compare GRPO against AsymRE for Llama 8B and Qwen 3B on MATH and NuminaMath; v1 contains no corresponding external-algorithm comparison.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, NuminaMath training/evaluation subsets of 142k/2k examples, and GRPO comparisons extending to 6,000 steps. The existing MATH settings, eight samples per prompt, rewards of +1/-1 and 250-step behavior-policy update interval are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Figures 9-12 substantially expand baseline-sensitivity testing: Llama 3B on MATH and all three models on NuminaMath. These curves test how baseline offsets affect learning and collapse across additional settings. The original entropy analyses and seven-run stability check remain.

E5.justification: The existing three-seed averages and seven independent runs per baseline are retained, including in relocated figures. The new experiments introduce no stated repeat counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds Llama 3B MATH results, three models' NuminaMath sensitivity curves, and GRPO comparisons on both datasets. The latter show especially faster convergence by training step for Qwen 3B under AsymRE, with smaller Llama 8B differences. Original results are retained; v1 Figure 8 becomes v2 Figure 4.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 and its Appendix A restatement correct the term mu(z)(r(y)-V) to mu(z)(r(z)-V) in the support condition for V > V^mu. This aligns the statement with the existing a_y-a_z-b derivation. The remaining proofs are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about baseline-dependent off-policy dynamics, policy improvement and conservative baselines preventing collapse. The expanded experiments do not redefine those headline contributions.

C2.justification: The diversity-collapse explanation, qualifications about transferring tabular theory to LLMs, and limitations concerning importance correction, KL regularization and multi-epoch efficiency are retained. The added GRPO passage reports results with a general further-testing caveat, without a new mechanism or concrete applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the added Llama checkpoint and provides a NuminaMath dataset-access reference. Appendix B's optimizer, learning rate, batching, sequence-length and decoding details remain unchanged; GRPO-specific implementation details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Degris et al. (2012) on off-policy actor-critic, Zhu et al. (2025) on positive and negative reinforcement, and the NuminaMath reference. Section 2 briefly distinguishes established off-policy RL research and on-policy sample-sign analysis from this work.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to related work, experimental setup, a short GRPO-comparison paragraph, appendix descriptions and theorem wording. The overall section structure and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 moves the Qwen MATH figure into the main text, combines the original collapse plot with a new GRPO panel in Figure 5, and adds the Llama 3B/NuminaMath dynamics and NuminaMath comparison displays in Figures 9-13. This substantially expands and reorganizes the experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support beyond MATH and supplies a previously missing GRPO comparison, while correcting Theorem 4.2's support condition. These are useful gains, but the new comparisons lack GRPO-specific implementation details and stated uncertainty estimates. Their convergence plots support comparisons by training step, rather than measured runtime efficiency, limiting the strength of the practical conclusions.
